venue.name: Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM)
venue.alsoKnownAs: University of the City of Manila
venue.description: A full campus of colleges, gymnasiums and the PLM Chapel behind its own gate, in the southern quarter of the walled city. Sessions run in several buildings across the campus.

buildings.name: Justo Albert Auditorium
buildings.notes: A single auditorium venue, not a multi-room building.

buildings.name: Gusaling Katipunan (Katipunan Building)
buildings.notes: Coordinate from a visitor-supplied Google Maps pin; not independently verified.

buildings.name: Gusaling Emilio Ejercito Sr. (Emilio Ejercito Sr. Building)
buildings.notes: A visitor confirmed both the AVR and KL rooms are in this one building.

buildings.name: Gusaling Don Pepe Atienza (Don Pepe Atienza Building)
buildings.notes: On the Muralla Street side; home of the College / Mass Communication Office.

localGuide.note: Places inside the Intramuros walls, from the Intramuros Guide map that hosts this chatbot. Every one is verified to sit inside the official boundary (OSM relation 103707). Walking times are straight-line from the venue at 80 m per minute, so allow a little more on the ground.
localGuide.priceCaveat: Food prices are indicative estimates for a typical meal per person, not quoted prices. Menus change — treat the band as a guide.
localGuide.feeCaveat: Entrance fees are from the Intramuros Administration and site operators. Discounted rates generally apply to students, seniors and PWD — bring ID.
localGuide.stayCaveat: Hotel rates are a dated snapshot, not live pricing.

passport.extra: Includes a free guided tranvía tour.
passport.note: Centro de Turismo is the fifth covered site; it is not pinned here because its coordinates could not be verified.

eat.name: 9 Spoons
eat.where: Muralla corner Victoria Street · The Bayleaf Intramuros, 9th floor
eat.about: All-day dining restaurant on the top floor of The Bayleaf, serving Filipino heritage dishes — kare-kare, bagnet, sizzling bulalo — plus a weekday lunch buffet. Shares its coordinates with the hotel building; no separate OSM node exists for the restaurant itself.

eat.name: Adams Canteen
eat.about: Neighbourhood canteen serving Filipino rice meals on the streets behind the southern wall.

eat.name: Aujen's Coffee
eat.about: Small independent coffee bar a short walk from Manila Cathedral.

eat.name: Bacolod Chk-N-Bbq
eat.about: Chain grill for Bacolod-style chicken inasal and barbecue skewers over rice.

eat.name: Bacolodnon Eatery
eat.about: Bacolod-style carinderia — chicken inasal and Negrense home cooking over rice. Not in OpenStreetMap — the coordinate is from a Google Maps pin supplied by a visitor.

eat.name: Balai Maria
eat.about: Filipino kitchen on the quieter western side of the walled city.

eat.name: Bamboo Intramuros
eat.about: Art-filled restaurant and bar on the northern edge of Intramuros — listed locally as Bambu Intramuros Art Bar and Restaurant — known for lechon kawali and cocktails amid bamboo-themed décor.

eat.name: Barbara's Casa Manila
eat.price: Fine dining — ₱1,000 and up per person
eat.where: General Luna Street · Plaza San Luis Complex
eat.about: Heritage buffet inside a Spanish-era mansion, with a Filipino cultural show at dinner.

eat.name: Bataka Bar
eat.where: General Luna Street · Plaza San Luis Complex
eat.about: One of the dining spots inside the Plaza San Luis heritage complex, a few steps from Casa Manila, serving Filipino plates alongside its drinks list.

eat.name: Batala
eat.about: Ice cream counter in the southern quarter of the walled city — a separate venue from Batala Bar below, despite the near-identical name.

eat.name: Batala Bar
eat.where: General Luna Street · Plaza San Luis Complex
eat.about: Craft beer bar and kitchen in the Plaza San Luis complex serving Filipino bar chow — crispy sisig, kare-kare, bagnet — alongside house-made ice cream and coffee, with vegan versions of several dishes.

eat.name: Beanleaf
eat.about: Coffee and tea house on the western side, busy with students and office workers.

eat.name: Belfry Café
eat.about: Café on Cabildo Street named for the bell towers it sits beneath.

eat.name: Cafe Intramuros
eat.where: Real Street · Plaza San Luis Complex
eat.about: Courtyard café in the Plaza San Luis complex, opposite San Agustin Church.

eat.name: Cafe Janealo
eat.about: Diner-style café serving rice meals and pasta, with live music some evenings.

eat.name: Casa Marinero
eat.about: Filipino dining room on Santa Potenciana Street.

eat.name: Casa Marinero II
eat.about: Second branch of Casa Marinero, a few doors from the original.

eat.name: Chamber Café
eat.about: Compact coffee spot on the western side of the walled city.

eat.name: Cheftain Eatery
eat.about: Turo-turo canteen with a rotating tray of Filipino ulam over rice; Google lists it as "Cheftain Eatery and Catering". Not in OpenStreetMap — the coordinate is from a Google Maps pin supplied by a visitor.

eat.name: Chowking
eat.about: Chinese-Filipino fast food chain — rice toppings, noodles and siomai.

eat.name: Cioccolata
eat.about: Coffee, churros and pastries at the foot of The Bayleaf hotel — one of four in-house dining spots at the hotel, alongside 9 Spoons, Raffaele and Sky Deck View Bar.

eat.name: Cioden's Diner
eat.about: Carinderia serving budget Filipino rice meals from about ₱35. Not in OpenStreetMap — the coordinate is from a Google Maps pin supplied by a visitor.

eat.name: Club Intramuros
eat.where: Bonifacio Drive · Club Intramuros Golf Club
eat.about: Clubhouse restaurant at the golf course laid out in the old moat, still within the Intramuros district.

eat.name: Cold Treats
eat.where: Real Street · Plaza San Luis Complex
eat.about: Ice cream and cold snacks stall in the Plaza San Luis complex.

eat.name: Dexter Pizza - Sisay's
eat.about: Neighbourhood pizza and short-order counter near Beaterio Street.

eat.name: Figaro
eat.about: Branch of the Filipino coffee chain on Andres Soriano Avenue.

eat.name: Flower Stories Cafe
eat.about: Small flower-shop café near Magallanes Street.

eat.name: Greenwich
eat.about: Pizza and pasta fast food chain on Andres Soriano Avenue.

eat.name: Ilustrado
eat.about: Long-established Spanish-Filipino restaurant in the walled city, known for paella and heritage set menus.

eat.name: J's Cuisine
eat.about: Casual Filipino restaurant in the northeastern quarter, near Anda Street.

eat.name: Jollibee
eat.where: Muelle del Rio · Near the Pasig River
eat.about: The country's biggest fast food chain — Chickenjoy, burger steak and sweet spaghetti.

eat.name: Kabayan Food House
eat.about: Turo-turo food house ladling out Filipino home cooking by the plate.

eat.name: KFC
eat.about: Fried chicken chain branch off Andres Soriano Avenue.

eat.name: La Cathedral Cafe
eat.about: Multi-storey café with a roof deck looking straight across at the dome of Manila Cathedral.

eat.name: La Events Cafe
eat.about: All-day breakfast and sandwiches on the western side of the walled city.

eat.name: Lacanilao's Tapsilogan
eat.about: Tapsilogan on Victoria Street doing the standard silog line-up — tapa, longganisa and tocino with garlic rice and egg — through the day. Not in OpenStreetMap — the coordinate was supplied directly by a visitor.

eat.name: Liezel's Place
eat.about: Carinderia serving Filipino rice meals near the southern wall.

eat.name: Los Frailes Cafe
eat.where: Real Street · Near San Agustin Church
eat.about: Café named for the friars, steps from San Agustin Church.

eat.name: Max's Restaurant
eat.about: The classic Filipino chain built on fried chicken, with full rice meals and sharing platters.

eat.name: McDonald's
eat.about: Burger chain branch on Muralla Street by the university campuses.

eat.name: MK Cookies & Pastries
eat.about: Cookie and pastry counter on Beaterio Street.

eat.name: Moonleaf
eat.about: Milk tea shop on Victoria Street.

eat.name: Papa Kape
eat.about: Coffee bar within the grounds of Fort Santiago, pouring Philippine-grown beans.

eat.name: Paper + Cup
eat.about: Quiet specialty coffee spot near the eastern wall.

eat.name: Parers Kimchi
eat.about: Korean kitchen serving kimchi stews and grilled plates near Beaterio Street.

eat.name: Pastil Sa Tabi (PST)
eat.about: Small pastil counter on Victoria Street serving cheap banana-leaf parcels of rice with shredded chicken or beef, to go. Not in OpenStreetMap — the coordinate was supplied directly by a visitor.

eat.name: Pastil-an Sayo
eat.about: Pastil stall at 729A Victoria Street selling banana-leaf parcels of rice with shredded chicken or beef, from about ₱25. Not in OpenStreetMap — the coordinate is from a Google Maps pin supplied by a visitor.

eat.name: Patio de Conchita
eat.about: Rustic carinderia set in an old Spanish house, known for complete Filipino rice meals at around ₱140.

eat.name: Pepito Foodhouse
eat.about: Grill house on Solana Street doing barbecue, chicken and rice plates.

eat.name: PLM Canteen
eat.about: Campus canteen at Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila, on General Luna Street. The visitor-supplied pin resolves to the PLM Multi-Purpose Building — confirm the exact spot and whether it is open to conference visitors.

eat.about: Wood-fired pizza restaurant on The Bayleaf's third floor. Shares its coordinates with the hotel building; no separate OSM node exists for the restaurant itself.

eat.name: Ristorante delle Mitre
eat.where: General Luna Street · Opposite San Agustin Church
eat.about: Catholic-themed dining room opposite San Agustin Church, known for very large sharing portions.

eat.name: Savor & Kribs
eat.about: Casual grill and Filipino plates on Victoria Street.

eat.name: Sky Deck View Bar
eat.where: Muralla Street · The Bayleaf Hotel roof deck
eat.about: Rooftop lounge atop The Bayleaf serving cocktails and bar snacks, with a view over the walls, the Intramuros golf course and the Manila Bay sunset.

eat.name: Starbucks — General Luna (North)
eat.about: Coffee chain branch on the northern stretch of General Luna Street.

eat.name: Starbucks — General Luna (South)
eat.about: Coffee chain branch on the southern stretch of General Luna Street.

eat.name: Starbucks — Muralla
eat.about: Coffee chain branch on Muralla Street beside the university campuses.

eat.name: Sunlai Foodhouse
eat.about: Food house near the southern wall serving Filipino plates over rice.

eat.name: Tesoros
eat.where: General Luna Street · Plaza San Luis Complex
eat.about: Café and dining room attached to the Tesoro's handicrafts store in Plaza San Luis.

eat.name: Vtan's Eatery
eat.about: Carinderia on Victoria Street with a short daily menu of Filipino home dishes over rice. Not in OpenStreetMap — the coordinate was supplied directly by a visitor.

eat.name: Zaqueo Sisigan
eat.about: Sisig eatery plating the sizzling chopped-pork classic over rice. Not in OpenStreetMap — the coordinate is from a Google Maps pin supplied by a visitor.

see.name: Ayuntamiento de Manila
see.feeNote: A working government building; interior access is limited
see.where: Andres Soriano Avenue · Plaza de Roma
see.about: The Casas Consistoriales — city hall of Spanish Manila, destroyed in 1945 and rebuilt in 2013 behind its original neoclassical facade. Now the Bureau of the Treasury.

see.name: Bahay Tsinoy
see.where: Anda corner Cabildo Street · Kaisa Heritage Center
see.about: Museum of Chinese life in the Philippines, run by Kaisa Para Sa Kaunlaran. Traces the Tsinoy community from pre-colonial trade through the Parián, the galleon era and the Second World War. Strong on primary material.

see.name: Baluarte de San Andrés
see.where: Muralla Street · South-eastern wall
see.about: A bastion on the south-eastern angle of the walls, one of the quieter points to get up onto the ramparts and see how thick the Spanish defences actually were.

see.name: Baluarte de San Diego
see.where: Muralla Street · Southern wall
see.about: A circular bastion begun in 1586 to a design by the Jesuit Antonio Sedeño — among the oldest stone fortifications in the country. Excavated ruins now sit inside landscaped gardens, and you can walk the rampart.

see.name: Casa Manila
see.where: General Luna Street · Plaza San Luis Complex
see.about: A 1980s reconstruction of an 1850s colonial merchant house, furnished room by room to show how a wealthy Manila family lived — from the caída and sala down to the paired lavatories.

see.name: Fort Santiago
see.where: Santa Clara Street · Northern tip, by the Pasig River
see.about: The Spanish citadel guarding the mouth of the Pasig, begun 1571 on the site of Rajah Sulayman's settlement. José Rizal was held here before his execution in 1896; brass footsteps trace his last walk across the courtyard. The pin marks the main gate, where tickets are sold.

see.name: Manila Cathedral
see.feeNote: Closed to sightseers during Mass and weddings
see.where: Cabildo corner Beaterio Street · Plaza de Roma
see.about: The Minor Basilica of the Immaculate Conception. The present building, finished in 1958, is the eighth on this site — its predecessors were taken in turn by fire, typhoon, earthquake and the 1945 battle. Belgian stained glass and a Dutch pipe organ.

see.name: Memorare — Manila 1945
see.where: Anda Street · Plazuela de Santa Isabel
see.about: Peter de Guzman's 1995 memorial to the roughly 100,000 civilians killed in the month-long Battle of Manila. A huddled group of figures beneath a grieving woman, with an inscription worth reading in full — the most affecting thing in Intramuros.

see.name: Museo de Intramuros
see.where: Arzobispo corner Anda Street · Reconstructed San Ignacio Church
see.about: The Intramuros Administration's ecclesiastical art collection, opened 2019 inside the rebuilt shell of San Ignacio Church. Colonial santos, retablos and ivory carvings, shown in a deliberately modern interior.

see.name: Plaza de Roma
see.where: Cabildo Street · Between the Cathedral and the Ayuntamiento
see.about: The main square of Spanish Manila and the natural place to start. It was a bullring until the 1790s, then Plaza McKinley under the Americans, renamed Plaza de Roma in 1961. The King Charles IV monument stands at its centre.

see.name: Plaza México
see.where: Aduana Street · Northern quarter, near the river
see.about: A square commemorating the Manila–Acapulco galleon trade, which ran between these two ports for 250 years and made Intramuros the hinge of the first genuinely global trade route.

see.name: Plaza Moriones
see.feeNote: Covered by the Fort Santiago ticket
see.where: Inside Fort Santiago · Fort Santiago
see.about: The old parade ground inside Fort Santiago, now lawn and acacia. The open space that makes the fort a pleasant place to sit rather than only to tour.

see.name: Plazuela de Santa Isabel
see.where: Anda corner Real Street · Central Intramuros
see.about: The small square that holds the Memorare monument, on the site of the Colegio de Santa Isabel — one of the oldest schools for girls in Asia.

see.name: Postigo del Palacio
see.where: Muralla Street · Western wall
see.about: The Postern of the Palace — the Governor-General's private gate to the river and the bay, small enough to be missed and carrying a relief of Our Lady of Solitude above the arch.

see.name: Puerta de Isabel II
see.where: Magallanes Drive · Northern wall
see.about: Opened in 1861 and named for Queen Isabella II of Spain, whose statue once stood before it. The newest of the original gates, cut to ease traffic to the river district.

see.name: Puerta de Santa Lucia
see.where: Santa Lucia Street · Western wall, facing Manila Bay
see.about: A western gate opening toward the bay, with one of the better-preserved stretches of curtain wall and a ravelin still in front of it.

see.name: Puerta Real
see.where: Muralla Street · Southern wall
see.about: The Royal Gate, reserved for the Governor-General and opened only on ceremonial occasions. Rebuilt in the 1960s; the sunken gardens beside it are a good quiet stop.

see.name: Rizal Shrine
see.where: Inside Fort Santiago · Fort Santiago
see.about: Museum in the barracks where Rizal spent his final hours, holding his manuscripts, personal effects and the original of "Mi Último Adiós", smuggled out in an oil lamp.

see.name: San Agustin Church
see.feeNote: The adjoining museum is ticketed separately
see.hours: Daily, roughly 8am–6pm (closed to visitors during Mass and weddings)
see.where: General Luna Street · Opposite Plaza San Luis
see.about: Completed in 1607, the oldest stone church in the Philippines and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It was the only Intramuros church left standing after the 1945 Battle of Manila. The barrel-vaulted ceiling is a trompe-l'œil painted flat in 1875.

see.name: San Agustin Museum
see.feeNote: ₱160 for students, seniors, PWD and frontliners
see.where: General Luna Street · Augustinian monastery, beside the church
see.about: The monastery beside San Agustin, now a museum of religious art, vestments and colonial-era furniture arranged around two storeys of cloisters. Quiet, and the best single introduction to Spanish-era ecclesiastical Manila.

see.name: Santa Lucia Barracks Ruins
see.where: Santa Lucia Street · Southern quarter
see.about: What is left of the Spanish infantry barracks, flattened in 1945 and deliberately left unreconstructed. The clearest surviving evidence in Intramuros of how total the destruction was.

stay.name: The Bayleaf Intramuros
stay.priceNote: From about ₱2,765 for a Superior; suites reach roughly ₱13,000. Typical standard room ₱4,000 – ₱9,100.
stay.where: Muralla corner Victoria Street · Eastern wall, beside Lyceum of the Philippines University
stay.about: The only full-service boutique hotel inside the walls. Operated by Lyceum of the Philippines University; also home to Cioccolata, which appears on the food map.

stay.name: White Knight Hotel Intramuros
stay.priceNote: Typically around ₱2,000 a night; standard rooms roughly ₱1,900 – ₱2,500.
stay.where: Plaza San Luis Complex, General Luna Street · Opposite San Agustin Church (mapped at Urdaneta Street)
stay.about: A 29-room boutique hotel in a restored Spanish colonial mansion in the Plaza San Luis complex — whitewashed walls, tile floors, wooden staircases. Has an in-house café.
